buyBody: A premium titanium hybrid at 19 degrees, built for speed and forgiveness on long approaches. High launch, mid spin, a neutral flight, and a Flex Channel face that keeps ball speed up when you do not catch it flush. Right or left hand.
whatYouGet: One Stryker LGH01 hybrid in the hand you picked
No headcover — none of our clubs ship with one
clubHeadline: The club that makes 210 yards a normal shot.
clubParas: There is a distance where a long iron stops being reliable and a fairway wood is too much club. For most golfers it sits somewhere around 200 to 220 yards, and it is where scores quietly leak away.
The Stryker is built for that gap. Nineteen degrees on a light 235-gram titanium head, with a Flex Channel face whose channels flex at impact to keep ball speed up on the strikes you do not center.

The shaft is stiff graphite, which keeps the head stable through impact without asking for a tour swing speed to load it. The grip is plain black rubber — the one restrained thing on an otherwise gold club.
The Glide Sole is the part nobody notices until they need it — less friction through turf, so the club moves the same way out of the fairway and out of the rough.

clubSpecs.v: Titanium hybrid, 19°. Not forged, not CNC-milled.
Flex Channel titanium — channels flex at impact for more rebound.
High, with mid spin and a neutral flight.
Glide Sole. Less friction through turf from the fairway or the rough.
Stabilised impact frame holds the head steady for tighter dispersion.
Anyone whose long irons have stopped being trustworthy.

videoBrief: 16:9 product film, 40–60s. The pitch is a distance, so film the distance: 210 yards from the fairway, ball tracked to the green, then the same shot struck off the toe to show what forgiveness actually means.

specTabs.aside: Stiff is the only flex offered. For a club aimed at the average golfer that is a real constraint, and worth knowing before ordering.

look.photo: Bold, full-bleed, portrait. Gold titanium head on the fairway at address, low sun. A hybrid is a wide, shallow shape — shoot it from behind so the width reads as confidence rather than bulk.
look.headline: The club you stop worrying about
paras: There is a specific relief in standing over a 210-yard shot and not running the numbers on whether you can actually hit the club in your hands.
In gold, with a gloss black crown, it is also the least apologetic long club we make.
look.aside: Everyone else is carrying the same club with someone else's name on it. It's better to be lucky.

closeBody: The Stryker is $209, right hand or left, in a run of a hundred. Sixty days to send it back if it isn't the one.

helpPick.headline: It goes in the bag where something else comes out
helpPick.sub: A hybrid earns its place by replacing a club you have stopped trusting. Which one depends on what you carry now, and the honest answer for most golfers is the long iron they already avoid hitting.

options.name: Instead of a 3-iron
options.body: A 3-iron and a 19° hybrid go roughly the same distance in the right hands. The difference is what happens in the wrong ones — the hybrid gets airborne from lies where the iron simply does not.

facts.v: Far better than a long iron

options.name: Alongside the driver
options.forWho: The second club off the tee
options.body: On a tight hole where the driver is too much gun, this is the club that puts the ball in play at a distance you can still reach the green from.

helpPick.note: If the gap between your longest iron and your fairway wood is a real one, this is a straightforward decision. Right or left hand, and sixty days to change your mind.
